---
title: "From RSEM files to a table you can plot, one pipe at a time"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

This page goes from a folder of RSEM files to the table a plot or a score needs. Every step takes a table and
returns a table, so the steps chain with `|>`, and each prints one line about what it did. To let you run every
line, it uses the three small RSEM files that come with the package (3 samples, 44 genes). With your own files,
only the first two lines change. All output below comes from running the code.

```{r}
library(rsemverse)

ex   <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "rsemverse")
dir  <- file.path(ex, "data")            # a folder with one *.genes.results file per sample
meta <- file.path(ex, "metadata.csv")    # the sample table: sample_id, ref (file name), and any groups
```

```text
data/        metadata.csv
  S1.genes.results      sample_id,ref
  S2.genes.results      S1,S1.genes.results
  S3.genes.results      S2,S2.genes.results
                        S3,S3.genes.results
```

## 1. Check, then read

```{r}
rsem_check(dir)
```

```text
rsem_check: 3 files; 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
```

`rsem_check()` reads every file and lists every problem at once (a missing column, genes in another order, a
different set of transcripts for a gene, non-finite values). It stops nothing; when it finds something, the
result is a table with the file, the check and the detail. Then read:

```{r}
tpm <- rsem_read(dir, meta, species = "human", expr = "tpm")
head(tpm, 3)
```

```text
rsem_read: 3 samples, 44 genes -> 43 rows (species = human, expr = tpm, org.Hs.eg.db 3.22.0)
  with symbol: 42 genes (1 symbols merged from several IDs); kept as original IDs: 2 genes

             S1        S2        S3
TP53   13599.42  16773.55  12812.60
GAPDH  18999.16  12154.88  12726.93
ACTB    3421.50   3993.31   3916.50
```

The result is a table with gene symbols as rows and samples as columns. The line above it tells you what
happened: 44 genes became 43 rows because the IDs of one symbol were **summed** (never the maximum), and 2 IDs
without a symbol kept their ID. `expr` chooses the value: `"count"`, `"tpm"`, `"fpkm"`, `"length"` and others.
Without a sample table (`metadata = NULL`), the files in the folder are found and each sample is named after its
file.

The table remembers what it holds, so the steps below need no `expr = `:

```{r}
attr(tpm, "expr")        # "tpm"
attr(tpm, "gene_ids")    # the original gene IDs behind each row
```

## 2. Look at the effective lengths before tximport or DESeq2

```{r}
len <- rsem_read(dir, meta, species = "human", expr = "length")
attr(len, "zero_length")        # genes with effective length 0, per sample
```

```text
rsem_read: 3 samples, 44 genes -> 43 rows (species = human, expr = length, org.Hs.eg.db 3.22.0)
  with symbol: 42 genes (1 symbols merged from several IDs); kept as original IDs: 2 genes
  genes with effective length 0: 0 in at least one sample, 0 in every sample

S1 S2 S3
 0  0  0
```

None here. In real data, genes with an effective length of 0 in some samples are the ones that stop
`DESeqDataSetFromTximport()`. `rsem_length_profile(len)` gives per gene the median and mean length, the
`zero_fraction` and `max_min_ratio` (how much the length differs between samples), so you can pick out the genes
to drop (`rsem_as_tximport(zero_length = "drop")`) or to take from transcript-level files.

## 3. Choose a detection threshold, then filter

```{r}
tpm |> rsem_detection_curve(thresholds = c(1, 5), min_samples = c(1, 0.5))
```

```text
rsem_detection_curve: 43 genes x 3 samples; 2 thresholds x 2 sample requirements (TPM)
  threshold min_samples samples_needed genes share genes_mean
1         1         1.0              1    43     1         43
2         1         0.5              2    43     1         43
3         5         1.0              1    43     1         43
4         5         0.5              2    43     1         43
```

Each row is the number of genes `rsem_filter()` would keep with those settings: TPM above `threshold` in at
least `min_samples` of the samples (a count if at least 1, a share if below 1). Here all 43 pass every setting,
because the example genes are all highly expressed; in real data the number falls as the threshold rises, and you
look for where it levels off. Then filter with the setting you chose:

```{r}
filtered <- tpm |> rsem_filter(min_value = 1, min_samples = 0.5)
```

```text
rsem_filter (detected): kept 43 of 43 genes (TPM >= 1 in >= 2 of 3 samples); removed 0
```

## 4. Keep the gene types you want

```{r}
protein <- filtered |> rsem_subset("human", keep = "protein_coding")
rsem_steps(protein)
```

```text
rsem_subset: kept 41 of 43 genes; keep protein_coding (genes per group: protein_coding 41)

[1] "read: tpm of genes"
[2] "filter: detected, kept 43 of 43 genes"
[3] "subset: kept 41 of 43 genes"
```

`rsem_subset()` keeps or removes gene groups: `"protein_coding"`, `"mito"`, `"ribo"` (ribosomal protein genes), `"hb"` (hemoglobin), `"sex"`, `"ercc"`, and
with a GTF file of the reference `"rrna"`, `"lncrna"` and other types. `rsem_steps()` lists what was done to the
table, in order. The table carries this list with it.

## 5. Counts: normalize and transform

For values that depend on library size, start from counts:

```{r}
logcpm <- rsem_read(dir, meta, species = "human", expr = "count") |>
  rsem_filter() |>
  rsem_normalize(method = "tmm") |>
  rsem_transform("log2")
```

```text
rsem_read: 3 samples, 44 genes -> 43 rows (species = human, expr = count, org.Hs.eg.db 3.22.0)
rsem_filter (edger): kept 42 of 43 genes (CPM >= 1260 in >= 3 of 3 samples and total count >= 15); removed 1
rsem_normalize (tmm, count): 42 genes x 3 samples; effective library sizes: S1 6587, S2 7145, S3 7827
rsem_transform: 42 genes x 3 samples; log2(value + 1)
```

`rsem_filter()` with no settings uses the edgeR rule for counts (the thresholds adapt to the library sizes: here
CPM ≥ 1260 because the example libraries are tiny). `rsem_normalize()` offers CPM, TMM, TMMwsp, upper quartile,
DESeq2's median of ratios and quantile; it equals edgeR and DESeq2 on the same input. `rsem_transform()` offers
`"log2"`, `"zscore"`, centering and ranks, and they can be chained: `rsem_transform(c("log2", "zscore"))`.

## 6. Quality of the samples

```{r}
qc <- tpm |> rsem_filter(min_value = 1, min_samples = 0.5) |> rsem_transform("log2") |> rsem_sample_qc()
qc$sample_summary
```

```text
rsem_sample_qc: 43 genes x 3 samples; PCA on 43 genes (PC1 69.2%, PC2 30.8% of their variance); spearman
correlation on 43 genes (detected), median between samples 0.938

  sample_id detected_genes median_correlation min_correlation most_similar rle_median   rle_iqr
1        S1             43          0.9392933       0.9383872           S3          0 0.03915251
2        S2             43          0.9168680       0.8953488           S1          0 0.42195828
3        S3             43          0.9177741       0.8953488           S1          0 0.18511442
```

`rsem_sample_qc()` knows the table is already log2 and does not transform it again. `qc$pca_scores` has the
principal components for a plot, `qc$correlation_matrix` the sample correlations; the summary gives per sample the
detected genes, how well it correlates with the others, its nearest sample and the relative log expression (a
sample whose `rle_iqr` is far above the others deserves a look).

## 7. Z-scores against control samples

To score samples against a set of controls, fit the reference once and apply it. Here S1 and S2 stand in as
controls (two samples are the minimum; use many more):

```{r}
meta2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("sample_id,ref,group",
             "S1,S1.genes.results,control", "S2,S2.genes.results,control", "S3,S3.genes.results,treated"), meta2)

tp  <- rsem_read(dir, meta2, species = "human", expr = "tpm") |> rsem_filter(min_value = 1, min_samples = 0.5)
ref <- rsem_fit_reference(tp, reference = "control", metadata = meta2, group = "group")
z   <- tp |> rsem_apply_reference(ref)
round(head(z, 3), 2)
```

```text
rsem_fit_reference: 43 genes, 2 reference samples (S1, S2); log2(value + 1); 0 genes with standard deviation 0
rsem_apply_reference: 43 genes x 3 samples against 2 reference samples; standard deviation 0: 0 genes (set to NA); ...

         S1    S2    S3
TP53  -0.71  0.71 -1.11
GAPDH  0.71 -0.71 -0.56
ACTB  -0.71  0.71  0.53
```

`ref` keeps each gene's mean and standard deviation in the controls on the `log2(TPM + 1)` scale. A later batch
on the same scale is scored against the same controls with `rsem_apply_reference(new_tpm, ref)`, so adding a
sample never changes anyone else's value. A gene whose standard deviation is 0 in the controls cannot be scored;
`zero_sd = "drop"` removes it, and the default sets it to `NA`.

## 8. Plot or share

```{r}
long <- protein |> rsem_long(meta)
head(long, 3)

protein |> rsem_write("tpm.tsv")                   # gene, gene ID, samples
protein |> rsem_write("tpm.gct", format = "gct")   # for GSEA and ssGSEA
```

```text
rsem_long: 123 rows (41 genes x 3 samples) with 1 sample column(s): ref (text)

  gene sample_id    value              ref
1 TP53        S1 13599.42 S1.genes.results
2 TP53        S2 16773.55 S2.genes.results
3 TP53        S3 12812.60 S3.genes.results
```

`rsem_long()` gives one row per gene and sample, joined with every column of your sample table (group, batch,
age and so on), the layout `ggplot2` wants. `rsem_write()` writes the gene symbol, the original gene ID and the
samples:

```text
gene    gene_id             S1          S2          S3
TP53    ENSG00000141510.5   13599.4209  16773.5477  12812.5954
```

## 9. With a GTF and with isoforms

Two things need files that the example does not include: the annotation your RSEM reference was built from (a GTF), and the `*.isoforms.results` files:

```{r}
gtf <- "gencode.v29.annotation.gtf.gz"
tpm |> rsem_biotype_profile(gtf, types = c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "rRNA", "Mt_rRNA"))   # share per type
filtered |> rsem_subset(remove = c("rrna", "mito_rrna"), annotation = gtf)                     # remove rRNA

iso  <- rsem_read(dir, meta, species = "human", expr = "tpm", level = "isoform")
main <- iso |> rsem_select_isoforms(min_tpm = 1, min_fraction = 0.1, rule = "all")
iso  |> rsem_isoform_usage()          # dominant share and entropy per gene and sample
```

`rsem_subset(remove = "rrna", annotation = gtf)` stops if the GTF has no such genes, rather than removing
nothing. The selected isoform values are the original estimates; to quantify against the selection, build a new
reference and rerun RSEM. For the whole folder at once, `rsem_import()` reads several values together and
`rsem_as_tximport()` hands them to DESeq2; see the [function reference](../reference/index.html).
